paragraphs: AI is now part of daily life, from chatbots and photo filters to online customer services. But as AI becomes more advanced, it also helps scammers trick people in new ways.

One major threat is deepfake technology, which can clone a person’s voice or face to make fake videos, images, or phone calls that seem completely real. Criminals can use it to ask for money, pretend to be friends, or create fake rental listings. These scams are becoming harder to detect because AI-generated content looks more natural. To stay safe, experts recommend checking the source of information, questioning emotional or shocking messages, and comparing stories on trusted news sites. Watching for unnatural speech or lighting can also help spot AI fakes.
Sharing information about scams and staying informed are key to protecting yourself in a world where seeing is not always believing.

paragraphs: AI is now everywhere – on phones, websites, and social media. It helps people, but it also gives scammers new ways to lie.

One danger is deepfake technology. Scammers can use AI to copy someone’s voice or face and make fake videos or phone calls that look real. They can ask for money or pretend to rent an apartment. These tricks are becoming more difficult to see.

To stay safe, people should check where information comes from, think before they act, and look for strange signs like robotic speech or strange faces in videos. Talking about scams with family and friends can also help stop them.

paragraphs: AI is in phones, photos, and websites. It can help people, but some people use it to lie. They can make fake voices and faces. This is called a deepfake.
A deepfake can look real. A person can call you and ask for money. But it is not your friend – it is a trick. Some people also make fake photos of houses for rent.
To stay safe, check things. Ask, “Who sends this? Why?” If something looks strange, stop and look again. Tell your family or friends if you see a scam. Be careful when you use the internet.
